## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

With no transcripts, the "narrative" is reconstructed from the **strategic actions and the shape of the P&L** across six fiscal years (FY ending March). The arc is clear and coherent:

**Phase 1 — Aggressive roll-up (FY2021–FY2022).** Nojima built itself from a ~¥523B home-appliance retailer into a diversified consumer-services platform via two large acquisitions: **ITX** (mobile-carrier retail; Japan's #5 phone retailer, making Nojima #2 by volume) and **Nifty** (legacy ISP / internet business). The FY2022 cash-flow statement carries the fingerprint: **¥74.4B of acquisition spend** (`acquisitionsNet` −74,423M) funded by **¥38.4B of new debt** — the most levered, most offensive year in the file. FY2021 also shows a one-off ¥29.98B non-operating gain (`totalOtherIncomeExpensesNet`), almost certainly a bargain-purchase/step-acquisition gain, which inflated FY2021 net income to ¥52.8B and EPS to ¥178 — **the source of the screener's misleading "EPS declined from 178 to 67" optics.** That was never recurring earnings.

**Phase 2 — Digestion & deleveraging (FY2023–FY2024).** Revenue kept climbing (¥626B → ¥761B) but operating margin compressed to a **trough of 4.0% in FY ended Mar-2024** (OI ¥30.56B) as the lower-margin mobile/ITX mix diluted the blended margin and integration costs bit. Management used the cash flow to **pay down ¥44.7B of long-term debt in FY2024** (`longTermNetDebtIssuance` −44,708M). The story here is "absorb the acquisitions, fix the balance sheet."

**Phase 3 — Operating leverage inflection & shareholder-return pivot (FY2025–FY2026).** This is the live chapter and the reason the name screens at all. Operating income re-rated hard: **¥30.6B → ¥48.4B → ¥57.7B**, with operating margin recovering from 4.0% to **5.9%** even as revenue compounded to ¥982.8B. Simultaneously the capital-allocation posture flipped from "acquire & delever" to **"return & signal":** a **3-for-1 stock split (Oct 2025)**, a **dividend raised above guidance** (year-end ¥10 vs ¥8 guided; FY DPS ¥20), a **completed ¥4.38B buyback** (Feb-2025→Feb-2026), an **immediately re-loaded ¥3.3B buyback** (Feb-2026→Feb-2027), and an **EBITDA guidance raise from ¥78B to ¥83B.**

**Growth drivers introduced vs dropped:** the M&A engine (ITX, Nifty) has gone quiet — `acquisitionsNet` swings to **+¥11.55B (a net inflow)** in FY2026, i.e. Nojima is now *harvesting/divesting* at the margin, not buying. Overseas expansion is the stated forward driver but is not yet visible as a distinct margin contributor in the consolidated numbers I can see (FMP returns `not_found` for both product and geographic segmentation, so segment-level claims cannot be independently verified). **Net:** the arc has moved from empire-building to earnings-quality and capital discipline — a constructive, not deteriorating, trajectory.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

Management's "claims" here = the implicit promises embedded in their actions (raise the dividend → "earnings are durable"; raise EBITDA guide → "demand is strong"; buy back stock → "the shares are cheap"). I test each against the audited numbers.

No spoken tone is available. I substitute **"revealed confidence"** — what management *did* with capital, which is harder evidence than what they'd have said.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: STRENGTHENING.**

Nojima has completed the hard part of a leveraged consumer-services roll-up: it bought ITX and Nifty, digested them through a margin trough, **deleveraged to net cash**, and is now harvesting **rising, cash-backed operating leverage** (OI +58% in two years) while pivoting capital to shareholder returns (split, above-guidance dividend, serial buybacks, raised EBITDA guide). On *real* numbers it is a **17%-ROE, net-cash compounder trading at ~1.3x book and ~6x FCF** — cheap, not distressed. The "deep_value / −100% MoS" tag is a **data-pipeline artifact** (JPY-as-USD fair-value bug) and should be disregarded entirely.

**The single most important thing the director must weigh before sizing:** *Is the FY2025→FY2026 operating-margin jump (4.0%→5.9%) structural or a late-cycle, weak-yen/appliance-replacement peak?* The entire bull case is operating leverage on a **structurally thin (~4% net), slightly-eroding-gross-margin retail base** — if demand normalizes or the yen reverses, that 5.9% OM can give back fast, and there is **no activist, no hard catalyst, and only timid (~1%) buybacks** to defend the multiple in the meantime. This is a **quality-at-a-fair-price, low-blow-up-risk hold** that lacks a *forcing function* — a re-rating depends on either an external catalyst (TSE-Prime pressure forcing larger returns; an activist on that ¥96B cash pile) or simply continued compounding, not on any imminent dated event.

CREDIBILITY_SCORE: 4 | TRAJECTORY: STRENGTHENING
